clue.text: Worthless types are many in total

indicators.note: the letter for many is placed inside the word for total

parts.note: a total is a sum
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so crosswords use it for many

explanation.surface: A complaint that good-for-nothings make up the bulk of some group.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is a contemptuous collective word for the lowest, most worthless people.

clue.text: Like a sovereign begging?

parts.note: as means in the manner of, like
a king is a sovereign ruler

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether a monarch might ever go cap in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone for money or favours is begging them, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Move all ten about seeking to be so evil

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the three words are moved around

explanation.surface: An instruction to shuffle letters, framed as seeking malice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges MOVEALLTEN; 'seeking to be so' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolent means wishing harm on others, an adjective close to wicked.

clue.text: Striker of French well over Britain

indicators.note: the French word is spread over the two letters for Britain, enclosing them

parts.note: bien is French for well
GB is the standard abbreviation for Great Britain

explanation.surface: A footballer from France, playing well, overlooks Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: BIG BEN is the great bell in the Westminster clock tower in London, which strikes the hours. 'of' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The bell strikes the hours, so a clue-writer can call it a striker.

clue.text: Propaganda by seizing everyone who is in hearing

indicators.note: the word by grabs and holds the word for everyone inside it

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: in hearing says the word who is taken as it sounds, written another way

parts.note: the word who, spelt by its sound

explanation.surface: Propaganda spread by capturing whoever is within earshot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy publicity or hype, close to propaganda in sense.

clue.text: Modern sound, if in hailing

indicators.note: the word if is placed inside the greeting

parts.note: hi is a hailing greeting
taken as written

explanation.surface: Recent audio fashion, as if heard through a downpour of hail.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-fi, high-fidelity equipment, was the modern way to reproduce music in the mid-twentieth century.

clue.text: Discover about the stuff of old boots?

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: made of the stuff of old boots

indicators.note: the word for discover goes about, around, the word the

parts.note: to learn something is to discover it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Finding out what old boots were made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathern is an archaic adjective meaning made of leather, the material of old footwear.

clue.text: Combination said to obstruct progress?

indicators.note: said shows the word for obstruct progress is taken by its sound

parts.note: to block is to obstruct progress

explanation.surface: A merger that people claim is hampering advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a combination of nations or parties acting together.

clue.text: Country lay out on continent? F- off, it's not that one

parts.note: to lay out money is to spend, which here gives cost

indicators.note: off says the letter shown as F- is removed

parts.note: Africa is a continent
the letter F, shown on its own with a dash

explanation.surface: A country spread out over a continent, then a coy curse, then a denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'F- off' looks like censored swearing; it tells you to remove F from AFRICA. 'it's not that one' jokes that the country is not on that continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a nation of Central America, so it is a country.

clue.text: The single pine for perfection

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, a single
deal is softwood timber, typically pine or fir

explanation.surface: One solitary pine tree held up as the perfect specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is a British word for pine or fir planks.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a standard of perfection, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Cereal heard with bewilderment

indicators.note: heard says the word for bewilderment is taken by its sound

parts.note: a maze is a state of bewilderment as well as a puzzle of paths

explanation.surface: A breakfast food eaten in a state of confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is corn, a cereal crop.

clue.text: Student is included in sea projectile

definitions.note: used as an adjective: relating to things thrown or fired

indicators.note: included in places the student and is inside the name of the sea

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea of northern Europe
L, the learner plate, stands for student
taken as written

explanation.surface: A learner is caught up in a missile at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner sign on British cars, so it stands for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballistic describes the flight of thrown or fired missiles, an adjective close in sense.

clue.text: Support warning layer

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table
a horn is sounded as a warning

explanation.surface: A hint of support plus a warning for someone setting things down.
explanation.definitionFit: A Leghorn is a breed of hen kept for egg production, so it is a layer.

clue.text: Members — once there were many in the party

indicators.note: the letter for many goes inside the word for the party

parts.note: the Libs, Liberals, were once a major British party
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: Party members recalling the days when membership was large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once there were' suggests a party of the past: the Liberals, now merged into the Liberal Democrats.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms and legs are members of the body, the older sense of that word.

clue.text: Flemish type could be no other

indicators.note: the letters of Flemish could be rearranged into another type of word

explanation.surface: A Belgian character who might be none other than the man in question.
explanation.definitionFit: Himself means that very man, as in none other than he.

clue.text: Cynical view of potato and salad

parts.note: murphy is an informal word for a potato
slaw, short for coleslaw, is a cabbage salad

explanation.surface: A jaundiced opinion of a potato and salad lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: MURPHY is Irish-derived slang for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: The rule that anything that can go wrong will go wrong is a pessimistic outlook.

clue.text: Pal drops Roger for Nick

indicators.note: drops says the letter for Roger is removed from the word for pal

parts.note: a pal is a friend
R is Roger in the radio alphabet once used

explanation.surface: A friend abandons Roger in favour of Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Nick is a name for the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is the Devil, and a fiend is a devil or demon.

clue.text: Tree producing a lot of fruit with no core

parts.note: M, a thousand, stands for a lot

indicators.note: with no core removes the central letter of the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: A tree bearing plenty of fruit that has been cored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core' is the middle letter P of APPLE, which goes, leaving APLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a deciduous tree, source of syrup and the Canadian leaf.

clue.text: View of gold in 9's neighbour

indicators.note: the heraldic gold goes inside the neighbouring country

parts.note: Panama borders Costa Rica, the answer to 9 across
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A golden view of the country next door to 9.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, unbroken view of a scene.

clue.text: Low satellite falling short

indicators.note: falling short says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the Moon is Earth's satellite

explanation.surface: An orbiting body sinking low and not reaching its goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow's moo is called lowing, so low is a verb for that sound.

clue.text: A clue Pam made up — but you can blame Gordius

indicators.note: made up says the letters of the phrase are put together anew

explanation.surface: The setter owns up that a clue someone called Pam invented is his fault.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius is the setter, so the Latin phrase for 'my fault' is his admission.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means through my fault, an admission of guilt.

clue.text: Creating anger over maximum flight distance

indicators.note: creating suggests making something new from the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Losing your temper over how far a plane can fly.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's range is the furthest it can fly without refuelling.

clue.text: Frank offence at Royal Academy

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scandalous display at a London art institution.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Academy is a London art body; 'Frank' looks like an adjective but is the singer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the American singer, so Frank is a fair first-name definition.

clue.text: Her dire condition created new contract

indicators.note: condition indicates the letters of the two words are put in a different state

explanation.surface: Her dreadful state has led to a fresh employment deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To have rehired someone is to have taken them back on, under a new contract of employment.

clue.text: There's something fishy in bad whisky …

definitions.meaning: a ... is a freshwater fish, the rudd
... is American slang for cheap, rough whisky

explanation.surface: Suspicion that there's something off in poor-quality spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-eye names both a fish with red eyes and inferior raw whisky.

clue.text: … upbraid bad beer outside this country

indicators.note: outside puts the jumbled beer around the letters for this country
bad signals the letters of beer are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, is the setter's country

explanation.surface: Telling someone off for serving poor beer abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' turns BEER into REBE, which goes 'outside' UK.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuke someone is to scold or reprimand them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: They say doll waited in line and got roasted

indicators.note: they say means the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Barbie is a doll and queued means waited in line

explanation.surface: A doll stood in a queue and got a scorching.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbecued food is grilled or roasted over an open fire.

clue.text: Very little info given by the heartless

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Scant information handed over by unfeeling people.
explanation.definitionFit: A byte is a small unit of computer data, eight bits.

clue.text: Brainteaser to some extent without difficulty

definitions.note: a phrase meaning with no trouble; the answer is the noun for that, as in with ease

indicators.note: to some extent says only part of the word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A puzzle that is solved, at least partly, quite easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is freedom from difficulty, so the phrase describes the noun's sense.

clue.text: Some early bishops rejected a female prophet

indicators.note: rejected says that portion is read backwards
some says just a portion of the two words is used

explanation.surface: Some of the first bishops turned away a woman who foretold the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes LYBIS from earLY BIShops; 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl was a woman of the ancient world who uttered prophecies.

clue.text: Not loud, or it would have been in the wind section

definitions.text: Not loud, or it would have been in the wind section

indicators.note: not says the letter for loud is taken away

parts.words: it would have been in the wind section
parts.note: a flute plays in the woodwind section
F is forte, the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A quiet instrument that would otherwise belong among the woodwinds.
explanation.definitionFit: The lute is a plucked string instrument, quiet, and outside the wind family.

clue.text: Paper can make you cross

definitions.meaning: the multiplication sign is a small cross

explanation.surface: A newspaper that might annoy you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry; it is the sign for multiplying.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times names a British newspaper, and the times sign is shaped as a diagonal cross.

clue.text: Screw container

parts.note: screw is British slang for wages, so this is the envelope holding them

explanation.surface: A box for keeping screws in.
explanation.definitionFit: A pay packet is the envelope in which wages, slang screw, were handed out.
